title: A Jigsaw on the Table
description: Piece together familiar words for a picture puzzle’s borders, tabs, and sorting work.
cardDescription: Piece together familiar words for a picture puzzle’s borders, tabs, and sorting work.
focus: This puzzle concerns the physical picture puzzle made of fitting pieces. A few answers name an edge or a corner, while others describe an action used to arrange the pieces.
solvingTip: Separate a piece’s shape from the completed picture. Use the short sorting and turning words to cross the longer puzzle terms.
words: Type of picture puzzle assembled from interlocking pieces
Puzzle piece position with two outside edges meeting
Outer band of pieces around a completed picture puzzle
Small projecting part of a jigsaw piece that fits a neighboring hollow
One separate fitting unit of a jigsaw picture
Outside boundary of a rectangular picture puzzle
Image formed when a jigsaw is completed
Container holding loose puzzle pieces before assembly
Shallow support used to keep a group of puzzle pieces together
To arrange loose puzzle pieces into groups
To match the shape and space of a neighboring puzzle piece
To rotate a loose piece while checking its orientation
Repeated visual design that can help identify matching pieces

answerNotes.JIGSAW: Jigsaw names the picture puzzle here. The same word can name a cutting saw in a workshop.
answerNotes.CORNER: In a usual rectangular jigsaw, a corner lies where two outside edges meet. Other puzzle shapes can have different boundaries.
answerNotes.BORDER: The border surrounds the image. Sorting edge pieces is one possible approach, not a rule every solver must follow.
answerNotes.TAB: A tab projects outward. The neighboring hollow receives it; the two shapes help pieces interlock.
answerNotes.PIECE: A piece is one unit in the assembled picture. Its shape and printed image both provide clues to placement.

title: A Cross-Stitch Sampler
description: Explore counted embroidery through fabric, thread, small squares, and the tools used for a sampler.
cardDescription: Explore counted embroidery through fabric, thread, small squares, and the tools used for a sampler.
focus: The clues introduce the vocabulary of counted cross-stitch without requiring a pattern to follow. Materials and supporting objects have different names, and direct definitions explain the specialized words.
solvingTip: Look for fabric, thread, a holding tool, or a counting action. Start with a short tool part before trying a longer embroidery word.
words: Decorative embroidery displaying stitches, designs, or an alphabet
Stranded embroidery thread often made of cotton
Four-letter name for evenly gridded cotton cross-stitch fabric
Ring-shaped frame holding embroidery fabric taut
Shape formed by two diagonally intersecting embroidery stitches
Thread-carrying hand tool used for counted embroidery
Fine strand drawn through embroidery fabric
To determine how many fabric squares a design spans
Regular network of small squares guiding counted stitching
One horizontal line of stitches in a sampler
One sewn unit forming part of an embroidered design
Threading hole in an embroidery needle
To form fabric stitches using a needle and strand
Woven material serving as an embroidery support

answerNotes.SAMPLER: A sampler can display an alphabet or examples of stitches. The word names the finished embroidery rather than the thread.
answerNotes.FLOSS: Embroidery floss is thread that can be separated into strands. Dental floss has a different use despite the shared word.
answerNotes.AIDA: Aida cloth has a regular grid useful in counted cross-stitch. The fabric name differs from the loose thread worked through it.
answerNotes.HOOP: An embroidery hoop holds the fabric while it is worked. It is separate from the fabric's printed or woven grid.
answerNotes.CROSS: The X shape gives cross-stitch its name. The clue asks for that shape rather than a religious object.

title: A Small Loom on the Craft Table
description: Explore a small loom through its frame, yarn, colors, and a simple woven mat.
cardDescription: Explore a small loom through its frame, yarn, colors, and a simple woven mat.
subtheme: A Small Loom on the Craft Table
focus: Threads cross over and under one another to make cloth. The clues use ordinary materials and actions.
solvingTip: Begin with a material, color word, or familiar hand action.
words: Frame used to weave threads into cloth
Outer support holding the weaving in place
Spun strand used for the small weaving project
Make cloth by passing threads over and under one another
Small flat woven piece laid on a surface
Fine strand crossing the little loom
One line of newly added yarn across the project
Curved turn of yarn with an opening in it
Feature changed by choosing a different yarn
Fabric made from the crossing threads
Pleasantly yielding to the touch, as some yarn is
Body part guiding the yarn across the frame
Draw a strand through the opening
Material used for many small loom frames

answerNotes.LOOM: A loom holds threads while others are passed across them.
answerNotes.FRAME: The frame provides structure rather than becoming the woven cloth.
answerNotes.YARN: Yarn can be made from different fibers.
answerNotes.WEAVE: Weaving interlaces threads rather than tying every crossing into a knot.
answerNotes.MAT: A mat is one possible simple project made on a small loom.

title: Beads on the Craft Tray
description: Explore small jewelry pieces through their shapes, fastening parts, and connecting materials.
cardDescription: Explore small jewelry pieces through their shapes, fastening parts, and connecting materials.
focus: These clues distinguish a whole necklace or bracelet from a small component. Everyday meanings provide a route into a few beadwork terms without asking about gem prices.
solvingTip: Look for something worn, a small connecting part, or a material. A hanging ornament and a fastening serve different purposes.
words: Fastening used to close a necklace or bracelet
Ornament hanging from a necklace chain
Small tube or bead compressed to secure jewelry wire
Small bead or component separating larger decorative beads
Gem that can form inside certain mollusks
Small pierced decorative object threaded onto a strand
To thread a row of beads onto a strand
Fine flexible strand passed through small beads
Thin metal strand used in some jewelry making
Curved closed shape used to connect jewelry parts
Small decorative object attached to a bracelet
Series of connected links used as jewelry
Gripping tool used to bend jewelry wire

answerNotes.CLASP: A clasp closes the jewelry. It differs from the decorative pendant hanging from a chain.
answerNotes.PENDANT: A pendant hangs as a decorative element. Its name describes that position rather than the chain itself.
answerNotes.CRIMP: A crimp secures a wire by being compressed. The clue names the fastener rather than a decorative gemstone.
answerNotes.SPACER: A spacer helps organize the arrangement. It can be decorative as well as keeping other beads apart.
answerNotes.PEARL: Pearls can be natural or cultured. Imitation pearl beads may instead be made from other materials.

title: Folding an Origami Crane
description: Explore paper-folding vocabulary through flat sheets, pointed corners, and a familiar bird model.
cardDescription: Explore paper-folding vocabulary through flat sheets, pointed corners, and a familiar bird model.
focus: This scene concerns origami rather than cutting and pasting a collage. Named fold shapes are described in plain words, and a few answers identify parts of a folded model.
solvingTip: Picture a flat sheet before the finished bird. A fold is an action or shape; a crease is the line it leaves.
words: Japanese art of forming figures by folding paper
Line left in paper after a sharp fold
Fold type resembling a trough when viewed from above
Fold type appearing as a raised ridge
Long-legged bird represented by a familiar origami model
To bend a paper sheet back over itself for a model
Four-equal-sided starting sheet often used in origami
Point where two adjacent edges of a paper sheet meet
Loose folded section of a paper model
One outer boundary of a flat origami sheet
Finished representation made from folded paper
Thin sheet material used for a traditional folded crane
Line joining opposite corners of a square sheet
Sharp projecting tip of a folded paper shape

answerNotes.ORIGAMI: Origami is a paper-folding art. The clue identifies the form of craft rather than a specific folding sequence.
answerNotes.CREASE: A crease is the resulting line. Fold can instead name the action that makes it.
answerNotes.VALLEY: A valley fold forms a recessed V shape from the chosen viewing side. A mountain fold appears as a raised ridge.
answerNotes.MOUNTAIN: Mountain and valley are viewpoint-based fold names. The words borrow familiar landscape shapes.
answerNotes.CRANE: The paper crane is a familiar origami figure. The clue asks for the bird rather than construction machinery.
